cards.text: This song comes from the sons of Korah, a family descended from Levi (1 Chronicles 6:1, 22). The singer is talking straight to God, and he doesn't even warm up. He opens with pure wonder: 'How lovely is Your dwelling place, O LORD of Hosts!'

cards.question: When it comes to the courts of the LORD, the singer says he's fine waiting. No rush at all.

cards.text: His soul longs, even faints, for the courts of the LORD. Meanwhile, right next to God's altars, some neighbors already moved in and set up house without asking ANYBODY.

cards.question: Who's found a home near God's altars, with a nest for her young?
The singer calls the people who dwell in God's house blessed, and he says they're ever praising Him.

cards.text: Then the song turns to the people whose hearts are set on pilgrimage. Friend, I didn't travel ANYWHERE for years, unless you count sliding from the front of a junk drawer to the back.

cards.question: The singer calls the people whose hearts are set on pilgrimage blessed. Where's their strength?

cards.text: On the road, these travelers pass through the Valley of Baca. And watch what happens to that valley when they come through.

cards.question: As the travelers pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of ___.
Even the autumn rain covers the Valley of Baca with pools. But after that, the travelers on pilgrimage wear out and turn back before they reach God in Zion.

cards.text: They go from strength to strength, all the way to God in Zion. Then, right in the middle of the song, the singer stops to pray: 'O LORD God of Hosts, hear my prayer; give ear, O God of Jacob.'

cards.question: In his prayer, the singer asks God to take notice of our shield and to look with favor on someone's face. Whose?

cards.text: Then he gets to the reason behind all this longing. Friend, this man has RUN THE NUMBERS.

cards.question: The singer says one day in God's courts is better than a thousand anywhere else.

cards.text: Next he weighs two places to be: the smallest job in the house of his God, or a home in the tents of the wicked.

cards.question: Then he compares two places to be. He'd rather be a ___ in the house of his God than dwell in the tents of the wicked.

cards.text: Me? I'd sweep crumbs off this bakery floor FOREVER before I'd go back to that drawer. Then the singer says the LORD God is a sun and a shield, and the LORD gives grace and glory.

cards.question: The singer says the LORD withholds no good thing. From who?

answers.text: Those who bring the most gifts
Those who were born in Zion

cards.question: The song closes with the singer speaking to the LORD of Hosts one more time. Who does he call blessed?

answers.text: The man who trusts in the LORD
The man who serves as priest
The man who builds the altar

findings.problem: The question asks who has 'found a home near God's altars, with a nest for her young,' and the right answer is 'The sparrow and the swallow.' In Psalm 84:3, the sparrow has found a home, and only the swallow has a nest where she places her young. The question gives both birds the nest-and-young detail, so the right answer isn't true for both. The singular 'her' also clashes with a two-bird answer.

rule.text: A card about two groups needs an answer true for both. When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'The high priest' can be argued as right. The high priest was an anointed one (Leviticus 4:3, 'the anointed priest'), and Psalm 84:9 doesn't say who 'Your anointed' is. A baker could reasonably argue the high priest fits.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The setup calls the first option 'the smallest job in the house of his God.' That rules out the wrong answers on card 16, 'priest' and 'ruler,' because neither is a small job, so it gives away 'doorkeeper.' Psalm 84:10 also never calls a doorkeeper the smallest job.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The smallest job' describes the doorkeeper in a way Psalm 84:10 doesn't. The text just says 'a doorkeeper in the house of my God.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
